message.content: Trade played a vital role in strengthening the powers of the pharaohs. The pharaoh relied on trade to expand Egypt's reach across the Mediterranean and the Nile Valley. He gained access to exotic goods that he couldn't produce domestically, and his court thrived as a result. They—merchants, diplomats, and officials—served the crown faithfully, ensuring that every deal benefited the state. The pharaoh's wealth grew, and he could fund grand monuments, military campaigns, and religious ceremonies. In return, the pharaoh offered protection to traders who traveled through his lands. They trusted him, and he trusted them, creating a cycle of mutual obligation. The people, in turn, looked up to him as a provider, which reinforced his divine authority. She—each queen who accompanied him—helped forge alliances with foreign kingdoms, and she brought wealth back to the treasury. They all worked together to solidify the pharaoh's position, and he, in turn, distributed gifts to keep them loyal. The pharaoh's power, therefore, was never solely his own; it belonged to the collective effort of those around him, and he acknowledged that without their labor, he would be nothing but a king without resources.
